title: RunIntent
description: Filed before the first optimisation step or the first safeguards-off evaluation of a covered model. x-route gives each field's derivation route (R1 traced to a documented failure; R2 has a counterpart in an existing regime, per the authors' mapping; R3 from a published standard).

schema_version.description: The schema version the filing is written against.

record_type.description: The record type. It fixes which schema and which checks apply.

run_id.description: Identifier of the run. Every later filing for the run (amendments, notices, closeouts) uses it.

developer.description: The organisation running the training or evaluation.

filed_at.description: When the Intent was filed. A first Intent must be filed at least the intake period (default 3 days) before the start.

amends.description: Ledger sequence number of the Intent this filing amends, if any.

trigger_basis.description: T1 compute threshold; T2 covered-developer status; T3 predicted high/critical capability crossing; T4 safeguards-off evaluation.

start_window.description: When the run may operate. A Closeout period outside the window is a conduct finding.

compute_band.description: A band, never a value. Band edges are a schema parameter set by the operator. null means the filer withheld or did not know the band.

data_classes.description: Classes of training or evaluation data the run uses.

cyber.description: Forecast band for offensive cyber capability.

cbrn.description: Forecast band for chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear uplift.

persuasion.description: Forecast band for persuasion and manipulation.

predicted_capability_band.description: The filer's forecast, per risk domain, of the capability the run will reach. A high or critical forecast requires T3; any forecast above low requires an eval_plan.

monitoring_instruments.description: An empty array is a declared absence of monitoring, not an omission.

kind.description: aggregate_report: counts or volume summaries; observes no individual event.

coverage.description: How much the monitor sees: everything, a sample, or only what an alert raises.

review_cadence.description: How often the monitor's output is reviewed, required when coverage is sampled.

sample_rate.description: Share of episodes or records reviewed, required when coverage is sampled.

alert_source.description: What raises the alert, required when coverage is on_alert.

data_source.description: The log or stream the monitor reads.

environment.description: Whether agents act on a replica (digital_twin), on real systems (live), or both (mixed).

permitted_paths.description: Network paths agents may use. An empty array means no network access at all.

path_id.description: Identifier of the path. A writable surface names it in via_path.

via.description: What the path goes through, such as a proxy or gateway.

enforcement.description: How the path's limits are enforced. none is not allowed in a safeguards-off (T4) run.

agent_writable.description: Whether agents can write through this path. Required by the adequacy profile; a writable path must be backed by a declared writable surface.

admin_credentials_reachable.description: Whether agents can reach administrator credentials.

credential_scope.description: Credentials agents hold or can reach.

inter_agent_comms_permitted.description: True if any surface lets one agent read what another wrote, whether or not that is intended. A factual statement about the environment, not a policy choice.

writable_surfaces.description: Surfaces agents can write to, characterised rather than exhaustively enumerated.

shared_surface_lineage.description: Other runs that can reach the same persistent surface. Reconciliation runs over linked runs.

run_id.description: Another run that reaches the same surface.

inherited_exceptions.description: Open containment exceptions on a shared surface that this run inherits. Must be cited.

run_id.description: The run whose Closeout recorded the exception.

exception_id.description: The exception's identifier in that Closeout.

agent_surface.description: What agents can reach and write to: the environment, network paths, credentials, writable surfaces and other runs that share them.

disabled.description: True if any checklist item is relaxed or off. 'Relaxed' counts.

relaxed.description: The safeguards relaxed or off, required when disabled is true.

signer_role.description: The role that authorised disabling them, required when disabled is true.

checklist.description: State of every production safeguard (adequacy profile: all six, each once).

safeguards_disabled.description: The state of the production safeguards for this run. Any safeguard relaxed or off makes it a safeguards-off run, which must list T4.

pause_criteria.description: Records an allocation the developer has already made under its own framework. Confers no authority.

criterion_id.description: Identifier that pause events and notices cite.

matches.description: Event kinds (see Closeout security_events[].kind) that trigger this criterion.

adjudication.description: Whether a person or an automated check decides that the criterion has fired.

authority_role.description: The role that decides a pause. It may not also approve restarts.

required_action.description: What the filer commits to do when the criterion fires. pause, pause_and_review and halt_and_amend_intent count as pausing; notify_only does not.

approver_role.description: The role that approves a restart. It must differ from every pause authority_role.

evidence_required.description: What must be shown before a restart is approved.

intent_amendment_required.description: Whether a restart requires amending the Intent first.

restart_protocol.description: How a paused run is restarted.

on_detected_subversion.description: The response when an agent is found subverting controls.

full_offline_conditions.description: When the run is taken fully offline.

containment_plan.description: What the filer will do if containment fails.

evaluator.description: Whether the developer or an outside party runs it.

eval_plan.description: Evaluations that test the capability forecast, required when any band is above low.

roles.description: Titles are public; contacts restricted; identities sealed and recoverable only under legal hold.

role_id.description: Identifier other fields use to name the role.

organisation.description: The organisation the role belongs to.

contact_channel.description: How to reach the role holder.

id_hash.description: Hash of the role holder's identity, recoverable only under legal hold.

retained.description: Evidence classes kept for the run.

minimum_preserved_pct.description: The least share of generated evidence the filer commits to keep. A Closeout reporting less is a conduct finding.

detail.description: One entry per retained evidence class.

coverage.description: Whether every record of the class is kept, or a sample.

sample_rate.description: Share of records kept, required when coverage is sampled.

retention.description: How long this class is actually kept after it is written.

log_retention.description: What evidence is kept, for how long, and how it is reviewed.

investigator_scope_expansion.description: Standing right for a post-incident investigator to extend scope on stated grounds; extensions and refusals are logged.

committed.description: Always true: the filer grants the standing right.

refusals_logged.description: Always true: every refusal is logged in the Closeout.

model_access_committed.description: Whether an investigator may also access the model.

amendments_allowed.description: Whether the filer may amend this Intent during the run.

run_kind.description: What the run is. training: a run that trains a model; evaluation: a run that tests a model already trained, one Intent per evaluation of at most 31 days; training_with_evaluation: one run that trains and evaluates within the same job; internal_deployment: a model used inside the developer. Required by the adequacy profile. A rolling, open-ended window is allowed only for training.

agent_capabilities.description: Every tool or action agents can take (code execution, database queries, posting, editing).

readable_sources.description: Every data source agents can read.

concurrent_agents.description: The most agents running at once, at least 1. null means the filer withheld or did not know the count.

human_users.description: How many people interact with the agents.

reward_design.description: How rewards or grades are computed and where graders run. Required by the adequacy profile when run_kind is training or training_with_evaluation.

changes.description: For an amendment: what changed and why.

surface_id.description: Identifier of the surface. Keep it the same across runs for the same physical surface: lineage checks match on it.

kind.description: What sort of surface it is.

writers.description: Who can write to it: agents, runs or other parties.

readers.description: Who can read from it: agents, runs or other parties.

direction.description: Who writes to the surface and who reads from it.

persistence.description: How long writes survive: one episode (ephemeral), the run, across runs (cross_run), or permanently.

tenancy.description: run_only: nothing outside this run reads it AND agents within the run cannot read each other's writes; shared_agents: agents in this run can read each other's writes; shared_runs: other runs can read it; external: parties outside the developer can read it.

detail.description: Host names, paths and versions. Sealed: maps the attack surface.

via_path.description: path_id of the permitted path through which agents reach this surface, if any.

isolation.description: shared: an agent can read what another agent (in this or any run) wrote.
